limitations: Fresh random programs: 2 or 3 of the 200 per seed, all 3 instructions long, also appeared in training by chance, so the unseen count is 197 or 198. No concept, multiply, loop or variant program appeared in training.
controller_results.json's held_out_collisions field sampled a stream without the branch curriculum and is not meaningful; training_audit_by_group.json replaces it.
Multiplication results wrap at 8 bits. Inputs are all 4-bit pairs and 4,217 8-bit pairs, not all 65,536.
Programs fit in 24 instructions and 8 registers, and rollouts here took at most 60 steps. Longer programs are untested.

This instruction set is small, and each field is copied from a program token, so much of the task is a learned lookup plus a zero test. It shows general execution of this ISA, not of arbitrary languages.
Executing a program is not inventing it, and the host still holds registers, feeds predictions forward, iterates bits and dispatches.
A fresh program screened as halting on 4 inputs could in principle not halt on others; none failed.
Controller and operators are separate models, not one shared-weight Transformer.
The test set grew after the first run's diagnosis: the curriculum and other loop programs were added in response to that failure, and were written by the implementer.
